title: Native entry whose run command exits immediately leaves composition up polling forever
reviewer: review-402 (independent reviewer agent, Claude — did not author the reviewed work)
head-reviewed: 550e07b2 (master; fix commit 550e07b2 plus card-move commit d83a3ea3, diff 19e4ffb6..550e07b2)
scope: internal/lifecycle/composition_orchestrator.go (waitEntryReady deadline + pidfile liveness), internal/lifecycle/composition_wait_ready_test.go (new), the TASK-402 card and its criteria evidence
summary: All three criteria independently re-verified: targeted tests pass (fast-fail 2.01s within its 60s ceiling naming pid + log path; timeout test ends at exactly 1.00s with 'not ready within 1s (ready_timeout)'; TestEntryReadyTimeout covers max-wins and the 30s default); full go test ./internal/lifecycle/ ok and go vet clean; make build plus an independent E2E repro (composition plan, exit 3 native entry, never-ready check, ready_timeout 60) failed in 2.39s with exit=1 naming pid and log path with the sibling rolled back — matching the card's recorded evidence exactly. Correctness traced: no goroutine leak (resultsCh buffered, WaitUntilReadyWithContext always returns), waitCtx derives from the parent with deferred cancel, pidfile/log paths match ProcessPlugin's, entry.Process guard covers native runner entries via materializeResolvedEntry, no sealed records touched.
findings: F1 (non-blocking): cancellation race can mislabel the error — a parent-ctx cancellation delivered alongside results yields 'health check not ready' instead of the cancelled message, and a propagated deadline gets labeled '(ready_timeout)'; cosmetic, behavior stays bounded
F2 (non-blocking): on Windows isProcessRunning is hard-coded false, so the liveness probe would fast-fail every native entry there; pre-existing platform stance shared with Up's already-running check
F3 (non-blocking): pid reuse degrades the fast-fail to the ready_timeout bound; still finite
F4 (non-blocking): entryReadyTimeout takes the max across checks, so a check's smaller individual ready_timeout is not enforced at its own ceiling; documented
F5 (observation): entries with zero health checks still skip the readiness gate entirely — identical to pre-fix behavior, not a regression
